title: Presenting to executives: risk, money, and one slide

videos.script: This is the last lesson of the course. Davi has a strategy, and now he has an hour with the two people who can stop it. The CTO, who asked for it. And the CFO, who pays for it. {{review}} His first draft opens with the architecture. The reservation module, the row locks, the queue they form under load. It is accurate, and nobody in that room asked for it. {{draft}} Executives ask four things. What can go wrong. What it costs. When it pays off. And what you want from them today. {{questions}} So the risk gets a price. Twelve big on-sales a year, an eight per cent chance that each one fails, and three hundred and eighty thousand reais when one does. That is an expected loss of three hundred and sixty-four thousand eight hundred reais a year, against a fix of forty-eight thousand. {{money}} Then it all goes on one slide, with the decision in the title. And in the review itself, every question the CFO asks is answered by a lesson you have already done. {{slide}}
